bullets.title: MU: JPM & MS expect major beat/raise Wed; HBM TAM raised, 100% cash return pledge
bullets.body: JPM and MS both expect Micron to meaningfully beat Q4F26 consensus ($51.33B rev, $31.72 EPS) driven by DRAM ASPs +20%+ QoQ, HBM4 >$1B shipped in May-Q ramping 2x faster than HBM3E, and DC SSD revenue likely >$5B. HBM TAM raised to 'easily cross $100B in CY27' (vs JPM model of $160B/$282B CY27/28E); SCA coverage stepped to 35-50%, locking in GMs above prior 62% peak. MU commits to 100% excess cash return post 12/9/26 CHIPS Act anniversary with FCF running $24B+ in Aug-Q.

bullets.title: HBM severe undersupply through 2028; HBM4 prices seen +100-150% YoY — bullish MU/NVDA
bullets.body: Citi models HBM bit demand surging +62% YoY in 2027E and +69% in 2028E, roughly doubling consensus estimates, with supply/demand deficit widening from -21% in 2027E to -36% in 2028E despite Samsung +50%, SK Hynix +67%, Micron +52% capacity adds. HBM4 12hi pricing projected to surge 100-150% YoY from ~$2/Gb in 2026E to $4-5/Gb in 2027E; de-spec described as tactical to maximize shipments, not sign of demand weakness.

bullets.title: AMD: $8.2B all-stock World Labs acquisition — AI talent/spatial-AI push to compete with NVDA
bullets.body: AMD agreed to acquire Fei-Fei Li's World Labs for $8.2B in all-stock, expected to close by year-end; Li becomes AMD EVP & Chief Scientist reporting to Lisa Su. Deal targets 3D/spatial AI for robotics and physical AI, positioning AMD to control software layer for next-gen AI workloads and compete with NVDA-Dassault alliance; Citi maintains AMD as favorite growth compute semis pick for 2026.

bullets.title: MDB: CEO CJ Desai departs to META; stock -18-26%; analyst day guidance raise unlikely
bullets.body: MongoDB CEO CJ Desai is leaving immediately to join META as Chief Enterprise Platform Officer, heading the Muse enterprise platform buildout; Dev Ittycheria returns as interim CEO. MDB reaffirmed Q3/FY27 guidance but the CEO departure one day before Investor Day significantly reduces probability of medium-term growth guidance raise. Jefferies and UBS both view the selloff as an overreaction but flag CEO departure as a near-term sentiment/valuation overhang; historical tech CEO departures average -5% day-of, -9% 60 days.

bullets.title: NVDA: $150B buyback boost ($235B total); Army contract win; AI security platform launch
bullets.body: NVDA announced a $150B increase to its buyback authorization, bringing the total to $235B through FY2028 — the largest in history. NVDA also won a U.S. Army contract and launched a double-layered AI security system (OpenShell + Nvidia Sentry) as cybersecurity becomes a top enterprise AI concern. Anthropic's IPO prospectus shows NVDA investing up to $10B in the offering.

bullets.title: META: Muse enterprise platform launch — agentic threat to DASH, SHOP, BKNG, ETSY, CRM
bullets.body: META launched its full enterprise tech stack (Muse agent, Business Agent, Muse API, Muse Code) connecting to Asana, Zoom, Intuit, Box, Canva, Slack. JPM Tech Sketch flags DASH (-8%), CVNA (-7%), RDDT (-5%), OTA names (ABNB, BKNG, EXPE), ETSY, CART, WIX, SHOP all dislocated lower on agentic disintermediation risk. META moves to top of HF sentiment axis; author notes crowd risk elevated but DASH appears most dislocated among 'AI agentic loser' baskets.

bullets.title: MRVL: Investor Day Oct 6 — $18B FY28 revenue, $15-20 2030 EPS, $10B+ Google custom deal
bullets.body: Citi and Jefferies both preview MRVL's Oct 6 Investor Day expecting materially raised targets: FY27/FY28 revenue guidance to ~$12B/$18B, 2030 EPS of $15-20 (100-200bps margin expansion), and $10B+ FY29 custom revenue anchored by a new Google agreement. MRVL expected to outgrow AI infrastructure capex at 40%+ CAGR over next three years; Maia 300 could ship 100-200k units in C27. Citi PT $275 (9.2% upside) on 28x CY28E EPS.

bullets.title: NFLX: Deutsche Bank upgrades to Buy (PT $95, -5% vs prior $100); Ackman and Hedgeye disagree
bullets.body: Deutsche Bank upgraded NFLX to Buy from Hold, cutting PT to $95 from $100 (37% upside from ~$69), citing valuation. Ackman is constructive, viewing the 50% stock decline as an opportunity to rebuild his position given advertising success and rising cash generation. Hedgeye, however, has NFLX in Bearish trend with buy/sell range $67-73, and the risk range framework flags it as a short.

bullets.title: HOOD: Goldman upgrades PT to $145 on crypto/prediction volume surge; +2.1% pre-market
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs upgraded HOOD with PT raised to $145, citing September crypto volume +21% MoM and prediction-market volume +17% MoM, plus a steeper rates curve supporting 2027-28 net revenue estimates. HOOD is up 2.1% in pre-market.

bullets.title: SHOP: MS upgrades to Buy with $192 PT on agentic commerce positioning
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley upgraded SHOP to Buy with a $192 PT, citing strong core business momentum with H2 acceleration potential, agentic commerce inflection, and ~1.5x EV/FCF/G valuation. MS views SHOP as well-positioned for the emerging AI agent commerce layer despite META Muse disintermediation pressure noted by JPM.

bullets.title: HPE: JPM OW maintained ahead of Networking Investor Day; $70 PT, Helios a $5-10B opportunity
bullets.body: JPM maintains Overweight on HPE into today's Networking Investor Day, expecting management to revise 3-year networking CAGR above prior +5-7% guidance (likely to 20%+) given the +25% industry CAGR. Helios opportunity sized at $5-10B in rack/switch revenue in out-years; currently in POC stage with orders expected later in C2026 and ramp starting FY27. HPE shares up +159% YTD.

bullets.title: AMZN: Wolfe bullish for Q3 — meaningful AWS margin upside (37% vs 34% Street), 48% growth
bullets.body: Wolfe expects AMZN modestly above Street on Q3 revenue with meaningful AWS margin upside (37% WRe vs. 34% Street) and 48% AWS Y/Y growth vs. Street 37%. AMZN shares underperformed S&P by 12-pts since July 30 EPS on AI agent disruption fears. Hedgeye and 22V maintain bearish/cautious posture on AMZN citing higher rates and macro.

bullets.title: VRT: +2.0% pre-market on Vertical Research buy initiation and BofA US1 list addition
bullets.body: Vertiv Holdings is up 2.0% in pre-market after receiving a buy initiation from Vertical Research and being added to BofA's US1 list.

bullets.title: CRM: Opco survey — 85% tested Agentforce but nearly half still in pilot; LLM disintermediation risk flagged
bullets.body: Oppenheimer's CRM survey shows 85% of customers have tested or deployed Agentforce, but nearly half remain in pilot/testing with production adoption and monetization uncertain. Key AI risk identified as workflow disintermediation — LLM platforms potentially capturing more of the interface and incremental spend. CRM remains a consensus short per Jefferies HF sentiment data.

bullets.title: WBD: Argus downgrades to Sell
bullets.body: Argus Research downgraded Warner Bros. Discovery to Sell from Hold at the current price of $30.90.

bullets.title: MSFT, AAPL, GOOGL, TSLA: Hedgeye #Quad2 framework — long MSFT/AAPL/META/NVDA, short AMZN/GOOGL/NFLX/TSLA
bullets.body: Hedgeye's Risk Range signals show TSLA and AMZN newly flipped to Bearish trend; GOOGL also Bearish. MSFT (495-519), NVDA (215-235), META (666-777), AAPL (330-344) all remain Bullish. The #Quad2 macro setup (Dollar Up, Rates Up) supports the longs while rate-sensitive and consumer-exposed names face pressure.

bullets.title: CHTR: Wolfe downgrades to Underperform ($118 PT); Starlink broadband and AI churn risks
bullets.body: Wolfe downgraded CHTR to Underperform with a $118 PT, expects cable sub losses of -2.4M in 2026 and -2.8M in 2027 from fiber/Starlink competition. T was upgraded to Outperform ($29 PT) as less competitively pressured; TMUS downgraded to Peer Perform. Telecom sector down -14.4% YTD vs S&P +12.2%; cable down -34.4%.

bullets.title: BE: +3.3% pre-market; Oppenheimer initiates at $24 PT (49% upside) on data center power opportunity
bullets.body: Oppenheimer initiated Bloom Energy (FCEL in the note, but BE referenced in pre-market moves) with a $24 PT implying 49% upside from $16.14, citing modular 12.5MW data center power blocks with native DC capability, a $3.3B backlog, and 10GW+ pipeline (~$45B). Capacity expanding from ~40MW to 500MW/year by FY29 targeting $1.5B revenue and $300M+ EBITDA; closed first two data center orders.

bullets.title: CVNA: +2.5% pre-market; Jefferies web scrape shows Q3 units tracking 39% YoY vs 23% consensus
bullets.body: Jefferies' CVNA web scrape shows Q3 retail units tracking ~39% YoY growth vs. consensus lows of 23% from July, with consistent outperformance throughout the quarter. Buy reiterated; Q3 unit estimates raised above consensus but below the web scrape to be conservative. Positive GPU read-through from KMX beat (retail GPU $2,105, down only $111 vs guided $200 decline).

bullets.title: SNPS: Agentic platform with 50+ customer engagements; Investor Day expected to guide teens revenue CAGR
bullets.body: Mizuho and JPM both flag SNPS's Autopilot/agentic EDA platform with 50+ customer engagements and GA expected by end-2026, with potential to triple core EDA TAM. JPM expects SNPS Investor Day to guide LT revenue in the teens with EPS potentially 20%+ including Ansys synergies and a new LT Debt/EBITDA target. SNPS is down 1.3% pre-market.
